interest: This document provides valuable insight into Japan's interwar quest to secure strategic petroleum reserves and alternative overseas oil supplies for the Imperial Japanese Navy prior to World War II. It demonstrates how Japanese commercial firms, such as G. Kato & Co., reached into South America to explore procurement of Colombian crude and bunker fuel, while highlighting the vigilance and informal intelligence-sharing role of American enterprises like the Tropical Oil Company operating in Latin America.
overview: This file consists of a Department of State List of Papers (docket sheet) for decimal classification 894.347, covering equipment, supplies, and fuel for Japan. The single document recorded, dated March 21, 1935, is a note reporting on Japanese efforts to procure crude oil and bunker fuel from Colombia for the Imperial Japanese Navy. It relays intelligence from an official of the Tropical Oil Company in Cartagena indicating that Kiyoje Shimada of G. Kato Co. of Yokohama was making commercial inquiries in Barranquilla, and directs researchers to cross-reference file 894.0003/184.

subfiles.about: A State Department list of papers entry recording Japanese commercial inquiries in Colombia for crude oil and bunker fuel for the Imperial Japanese Navy.
subfiles.summary: This list of papers entry records a note dated March 21, 1935, regarding the potential export of crude oil from Colombia for refining and bunker fuel for the Imperial Japanese Navy. An official of the Tropical Oil Company stationed in Cartagena reported that Kiyoje Shimada, representing G. Kato Co. of Yokohama, was conducting inquiries in Barranquilla regarding oil acquisitions. The entry directs readers to related documentation under decimal file 894.0003/184.
